newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says certain of timely, hard euro.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says certain of timely, hard euro.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Tuesday that he was confident Europe's plannned single currency would begin on time and that the aim was to ensure the creation of a hard European currency.

In the summary of a speech to be delivered later today at the German American Chamber of Commerce in New York, Kohl was quoted by the government press office as saying: "Monetary union will begin as agreed on time on January 1, 1999. The clear goal is to create a lasting, hard single European currency. The stability criteria contained in the Maastricht treaty are not negotiable."
Commenting on the German economy, Kohl said the outlook for 1997 and 1998 was positive. He repeated the government's forecast of 2.5 percent economic growth this year.
He said Germany would continue to push through economic reforms aimed at making it more attractive for investment.
